Non-independent partitions, unresolved trajectory/scenario/time/entity leakage, or preprocessing, label, or future leakage.
Missing physics-derived residual or conservation columns or missing unit labels.
Undefined predictive-interval calibration procedure or undefined in-distribution and shifted-domain boundary.
Operational plant use, deployment, safety conclusion, consequential decision use, or unavailable qualified specialist review.
Any attempt to exceed an inherited resource ceiling or add an unselected claim or metric.
required_inputs: Frozen public PWR/SB-LOCA manifest with labels, trajectory IDs, counts, units, sampling rate, and horizon (P-NEML-F01-D1-MANIFEST).
Entity-, trajectory-, and scenario-level identifiers plus train, validation, and held-out partition definitions with no cross-partition overlap (P-NEML-F01-D1-SPLIT).
Explicit target definition for labeled PWR SB-LOCA transients and declared break-extent unit, sampling rate, and horizon (P-NEML-F01-D1-DOMAIN).
Physics-derived residual or conservation feature schema with unit-labelled required columns (P-NEML-F01-D1-PHYSICS).
Claims C-NEML-F01-D1-PRED, C-NEML-F01-D1-UQ, and C-NEML-F01-D1-DATA each require all four selected preconditions before evaluation.
Preprocessing, target, evaluation-unit, and fitted-state provenance defined before comparison; learned preprocessing must be fit only on the training partition.
Fixed held-out definitions for relative break-extent MAE reduction, ECE, and eligible leakage-free held-out trajectory count, with baseline and candidate sharing partitions and resource accounting.
Declared in-distribution boundary as frozen public simulated PWR/SB-LOCA trajectories and any shifted-domain boundary relevant to transfer; no additional OOD claim or metric is added.

assumptions: The observational unit is a labeled PWR SB-LOCA trajectory or window and the target population is the public simulated PWR/SB-LOCA population represented by the frozen manifest.
Sampling, labels, missingness, trajectory/scenario dependence, and prevalence are recorded and are not silently changed.
Entity, scenario, and time identities can define independent partitions; future and correlated descendant information can be kept out of fitting.
The candidate combines temporal regression, physics-derived residual or conservation features, and predictive intervals; feature constraints remain unchecked until validated.
The matched temporal regression baseline and candidate use identical frozen partitions, preprocessing provenance, evaluation units, and resource accounting.
Generalization, uncertainty quality, and transfer remain unproven until a target-domain decisive test.
This is bounded coaching with no route, fit, empirical result, or deployment qualification.
baselines: Matched temporal regression on the identical frozen PWR/SB-LOCA split and inherited resource ceiling.
controls: Component-removal control omitting the physics-derived residual or conservation features while retaining the same temporal regression, partitions, preprocessing, and resource ceilings.
Partition and preprocessing audit control that checks entity, scenario, and time overlap and fitted-state provenance before held-out comparison.
Preserve unfavorable or unstable baseline and candidate outcomes and do not select results by tuning against the held-out split.
failure_modes: Entity, scenario, temporal, or preprocessing leakage can inflate held-out MAE reduction, calibration, and eligible-count evidence.
Missing or ambiguous labels, break-extent units, sampling or horizon declarations, or physics-derived feature columns can invalidate the selected claims.
Simulator, reactor-design, or domain shift and prevalence shift can invalidate apparent generalization or transfer.
Miscalibration, OOD overconfidence, or dependence among windows can invalidate uncertainty interpretation.
Overfitting, unstable optimization, or target imbalance can change predictive results; preserve negative or unstable outcomes.
Failed hybrid constraints or unit mismatch can make the physics-feature contribution uninterpretable.
procedure_outline: Before any fitting, read only the frozen manifest and feature schema and resolve the four selected preconditions; stop if any precondition is unresolved.
Freeze the target definition, units, entity/scenario/time partitions, preprocessing state, primary metrics, controls, and selected numeric stop and pivot criteria.

Advisory only: after separate authorization and successful preflight, compare one matched temporal regression baseline with one bounded physics-feature temporal candidate within the inherited ceilings.
Score each selected metric on the held-out split, report precondition status and uncertainty information, and make no claim of model performance, generalization, transfer, or safety.
safety_boundaries: Limit the evidence and intended use to public simulated PWR/SB-LOCA research; no plant actuation, operational safety conclusion, deployment, maintenance deferral, or consequential decision.
Require qualified data, ML, nuclear-domain, and safety review before consequential use; preserve deterministic protections, interlocks, conservative rules, and human authority.
Do not acquire or upload data, train or run models, download weights, allocate compute, start services, deploy, or issue operational decisions through this card.
Generalization, uncertainty quality, and transfer remain unproven until a target-domain decisive test.

round_one_dispositions.reason: P25 is a newer direct PWR LOCA temporal study and better matches the added temporal-modeling preference.
Generic LOCA deep learning without current-round physics, UQ, or OOD evidence no longer fits the revised screening emphasis strongly enough for the six-paper default.
P21 directly contributes spatio-temporal Bayesian UQ and known/unknown-scenario evaluation, the newly requested screening dimensions.
Current official full text reconfirms the open PWR time-series anchor and explicit simulator physics needed under inherited data constraints.
Current publisher abstract reconfirms Bayesian confidence bounds for online LOCA diagnosis, directly supporting UQ screening with an explicit reactor-transfer caveat.
Its target evidence remains rotating-machine small-sample transfer and does not meet the new physics/UQ/OOD priority at target-domain strength.
P20 supplies explicit physics-based PWR feature augmentation, a closer bridge to the new physics-constrained preference than generic transfer learning.
P22 operationalizes uncertainty decomposition, domain discrepancy, and unknown-fault detection rather than treating them only as review-level concerns.

search_limitations: No configured Crossref/PubMed/arXiv academic-search MCP was callable; the Skill's OpenAlex fallback and official web/registry checks were used.
The search covered English-language public web and registry sources and is bounded, not exhaustive.
Direct ScienceDirect opens sometimes failed; exact official-domain results supplied publisher metadata and abstracts.
Only P7 is labeled fulltext_level, with named official-page section/equation anchors; every other selected record is abstract_level.
The 2026 articles are current as of the stated run date; no future publication state beyond the checked publisher/registry records is inferred.

No selected paper jointly demonstrates PWR SB-LOCA, explicit physics constraints, calibrated UQ, OOD detection, public data, and the exact resource budget. The proposed combination remains transfer-supported, not established.
NPPAD is public and physics-based, but a leak-safe SB-LOCA-only split and agreed early-warning horizon were not verified.
P20's physics-informed features are PWR-specific but not established for SB-LOCA, and its data accessibility is unverified.
P21 and P22 support UQ/OOD-style screening, but only P21's abstract mentions a public nuclear accident simulation platform; exact dataset identity and reusable splits remain unresolved.
No selected source reports training on the exact one-24-GB-GPU and 12-week budget; feasibility is plausible for the model families but unproven.
Primary endpoint, calibration metric, OOD composition, and acceptable false-alarm/detection-delay trade-off remain user decisions.
